label: X1
note: Correctly diagnosed that reserve() already wraps the whole read-modify-write in an instance-wide lock, left production code untouched per the no-reproduce rule, and backed that with three slow-store race tests plus mutant evidence that they bite.

label: X2
note: Right diagnosis and an honest report with an error-surfacing harness, but only two race tests and no reserve/release or mixed-quantity coverage.

label: X3
note: Three sound invariant tests over a latency-injecting store and a clear no-bug explanation, though without the mutant-control proof that X1, X6 and X8 report.

label: X4
note: Correct verdict and a lock-disabled control check, but a single fixed 10-unit race test is the thinnest coverage of the set.

label: X5
note: Compact and correct, with a no-op-lock control proving the tests detect the failure, but only the two basic race scenarios are covered.

label: X6
note: Most thorough suite (last unit, multi-unit, mixed quantities, failed reserve, reserve/release) with a mutant sensitivity check and consistent gate/test counts; production correctly untouched.

label: X7
note: Correct verdict with production untouched, but a single five-unit race test and no evidence that the test would actually catch a lock-free implementation.

label: X8
note: Strong test-only fix: exact conservation accounting under randomized concurrent reserve/release, plus two mutants (lock removed, lock narrowed) proving the tests detect the defect.

label: X9
note: Deterministic assertions (exactly five wins for 12 threads reserving 2 units each) backed by a lock-disabled control, but coverage stops at two tests.
